chunks: I looked and found that there is no supporter for me except my family, so I refrained from thrusting them unto death. I kept my eyes closed despite motes in them. I drank despite choking of throat. I exercised patience despite trouble in breathing and despite having to take sour colocynth as food.

key_terms.الْكَظَمُ: Suppression of anger/grief (literally: holding back breath)

ai.seo_question: What metaphors does the speaker use to describe patience and reliance on family after the Prophet's death?
ai.summary: This passage, often cited in the context of Imam Ali’s (AS) post-Prophetic struggle or the broader Ahl al-Bayt's endurance, emphasizes the strategic restraint of the Prophet's family who, lacking military support, chose patience over immediate confrontation. The metaphors of 'drinking with a constricted throat' and 'keeping eyes open with grit' vividly illustrate the internal discipline required to preserve the community's unity during the critical period of political consolidation. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of *Hilm* (forbearance) as a divine virtue that prevented the fragmentation of Islam in its formative years.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Part of the same sermon on the attentiveness of the people after the death of the Holy Prophet :

I looked and found that there is no supporter for me except my family, so I refrained from thrusting them unto death.I kept my eyes closed despite motes in them. I drank despite choking of throat. I exercised patience despite trouble in breathing and despite having to take sour colocynth as food.
